items.title: New VU1 compiler for faster games
items.text: The new compiler for the PS2's vector unit 1 gains many optimizations and now builds its code on a background thread, with the existing compiler as fallback. It also saves what it compiled on disk so later runs start faster.

items.title: Faster vector unit emulation
items.text: Many small improvements to the recompiled vector unit code do the same work with fewer instructions, so games that lean on it run a little faster.

items.title: Vector unit interpreter timing matches console
items.text: The vector unit interpreter now handles a branch after two writes to the same register, a read that must wait for a load, and the end of a program the way the real console does.

items.title: Empty vector unit writes now match console
items.text: A vector unit instruction that writes no fields no longer changes registers on the recompiler, matching the interpreter and the console.

items.title: Save states load correctly with MTVU
items.text: Loading a save state while VU1 runs on its own thread (MTVU) no longer swaps VU1's memory back to what it held before the load.

items.title: Faster texture cache and drawing
items.text: Paletted textures are matched by cheaper block hashes, uploads reuse work already done and the texture cache holds more entries, which cuts per-frame work in texture-heavy scenes such as Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance.

items.title: Faster software renderer copies
items.text: The software renderer copies paletted texture sprites into 16-bit frames straight from memory, which helps games like Spider-Man 3 that redraw thousands of tiny sprites a frame.
